workstream: qgraph merge verification: the merged default search path and the recommended opt-in encoding, one clean paired held-out run per dataset
method: public-bench ann-qgraph --index vertex --holdout 2000 (train vectors held out as queries, exact cosine truth; test.f32 and neighbors.i32 not read). Graphs: degree 64 (nytimes) / 32 (glove), build_ef 200, alpha 1.0, seed 0x5EED; E and D load the same graph through the checked cache (header: n, dim, degree, build_ef, alpha, seed, data fingerprint; format HMSGRF02); A (old binary) loads the same-parameter graph it built itself. All processes started with --sync; one timed.sh lock held a coordinator that rotated A, E, D round by round (round r starts at process r mod 3), RAYON_NUM_THREADS=3, searches single-threaded one query at a time over the 2,000 held-out queries. Load recorded before every step.
decision_rules:
(written before the runs):
 (a) the new default path (E) "loses beyond noise" to A at a target when the median paired
     E/A QPS ratio over the rounds is below 1 and E is slower in at least 10 of 11 rounds
     (two-sided sign test p < 0.05); the paired ratio is taken row for row, which is exact
     because A and E share the graph and the encoding (identical recall rows are checked).
 (b) the recommended encoding (D) "wins" over the default encoding at a target when the median
     paired ratio of the log-interpolated QPS at that exact recall is above 1 and D is faster
     in at least 10 of 11 rounds; it is adopted only if it wins at both targets on both sets.

On glove the A and E rows are identical. On nytimes E's recall is higher by at most 0.0006 with at most 4 more code estimates per query at the same ef: the new default path quantizes the query differently (split scales), which the earlier run ny1 showed on the very same cache file, so the graphs are the same and the difference is in the search code.
